correctness.rationale: The fixed-point equation is inverted through the odd increasing H(m)=m+sqrt(epsilon)m/sqrt(phi^2-m^2), whose positive half has positive second derivative. Its strictly concave inverse h gives a unique zero of 2h(x+a)+h(x-2a) in (-a,0). The memory-sum identity yields the unique monotone scalar root p and exact reconstructed x. Three separate singular expansions produce, respectively, persistent shift with universal sqrt(epsilon/3) correction, the critical cube-root coefficient (phi/36)^(1/3), and the supercritical sqrt(epsilon) coefficient. The Jacobian eigenvalue argument gives local attraction under the stated sufficient beta and eta bounds. The embedded checker numerically tests 1011 finite identities but does not prove the universal theorem.

value.rationale: The result isolates a natural implementation tradeoff in error-feedback robust optimization: even strictly convex equal-curvature noise-free objectives can have a locally attracting biased fixed point when clipping parameters do not decay. It identifies the exact clipping threshold 2a and the nonuniform limiting rates including a critical epsilon^(1/3) boundary layer, rather than a mere one-parameter counterexample. It proves that two clients cannot exhibit this mechanism within the specified natural equal-curvature class and supplies exact algebraic parameters for reproducible stress tests. It neither overclaims broader convergence nor requires downstream theorems to make this structural classification useful.
